comparator.name: Linguistics
comparator.sourceNotes: Revisit of unchanged2026–2027 formal regulations confirms180listedEC for September2026entry:60B1+60B2+30minor+30portfolio, three of five10EC seminars. The compulsory10EC PsycholinguisticsProject is not the catalogue’s old5EC Psycholinguistics course; Art7.1 does not explicitly reconcile their entry treatment. Neurolinguistics and developmental-language-disorders seminars still name older prerequisites, including StatisticsII and clinical subcourses. Catalogue transition notes confirm shared teaching of old/new clinical and phonology/syntax modules for earlier cohorts, not a prospective entry waiver for the new cohort. Retain listed credits and withhold progression/comparison approval. All three portfolio seminars must pass and their unrounded mean must be at least5.5. Individual replacement research is a conditional last-component remedy under Art7.4, not an unrestricted alternative programme.

exception.reason: The September 2026 Linguistics curriculum requires a 10 EC Psycholinguistics Project and three graduation seminars. The current catalogue still lists the earlier 5 EC Psycholinguistics course and older prerequisites for the Neurolinguistics and developmental-language-disorders seminars. Applicable entry rules or adopted equivalences for the redesigned cohort remain unverified.
exception.curriculumContext: Current PartB Articles4.1/5.1(a) support60EC first year,60EC second year and30EC minor plus three10EC portfolio seminars=180EC. Article7.1 names Psycholinguistics after Statistics, but does not identify the new10EC project; current catalogue still describes an earlier5EC course and older StatisticsII/clinical entry. ClinicalLinguistics explicitly changes entry to LanguageAndSpeechDisorders from2027–2028. The current transition scheme describes earlier clinical/first-year subcourses sharing newer teaching, but does not give a prospective project/seminar entry equivalence. AssessmentPlan preserves written assignment, poster and presentation; no unavailable rule is inferred.

audience.programmeDescription: Groningen’s Dutch-taught Linguistics bachelor studies how people learn and use language, how languages are structured, and what happens when language is affected by a disorder.

curriculum.limitation: The listed courses account for 180 EC. Entry to the required Psycholinguistics Project and two selected graduation seminars has not yet been verified for students starting in September 2026.
